title: Don't be a meat proxy
author: ngruhn
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Too often I ask a question in Slack or leave feedback under a merge/pull request or argue with friends in a WhatsApp group and get back:

Please don't do this. I mean, I've done this. But I've been on the receiving end too many times now. This is not adding value. I can talk to Claude myself. It's going to be faster and I get to control the context. I don't need a meat proxy in between.
Reading AI output is extra effort. It's verbose, frequently contains all too plausible nonsense, and is increasingly jargon dense. I recently got this sentence from Claude:
summaryZh: Too often I ask a question in Slack or leave feedback under a merge/pull request or argue with friends in a WhatsApp group and get back:

comments.author: eddythompson80
comments.textRawHtml:
I deal with this all day long at work and it’s exhausting. People almost acting like no one has thought of it “I asked Claude what happened, and it spit out this 300 line response. Can you read it for me and see if it’s right?”

What kills me is you might expect this from a busy high level manager that doesn’t really understand the technical details and they just point the AI to an error they got. They don’t know how to interpret the response, so they ask someone who work on the thing. It’s still kinds annoying because you could just ask, but whatever. But to get these from junior and senior engineer for the areas they work in and expect someone else to read it for them? It’s crazy behavior. How can someone serious even think that’s ok.
comments.textZhHtml:
我在工作中整天处理这个问题，这让人筋疲力尽。人们几乎表现得好像没有人想到过“我问 Claude 发生了什么事，它吐出了 300 行的回复。你能为我读一下它，看看它是否正确吗？”

让我丧命的是，你可能会认为这是一位忙碌的高层经理提出的，但他并不真正了解技术细节，他们只是将 AI 指向他们遇到的错误。他们不知道如何解释这个回应，所以他们询问从事这件事的人。这仍然有点烦人，因为你可以直接问，但无论如何。但是要从他们工作领域的初级和高级工程师那里获取这些内容并期望其他人为他们阅读？这是疯狂的行为。认真的人怎么可能认为这没关系。

children.author: ffsm8
children.textRawHtml:
At my dayjob there is a person spearheading ai across the enterprise.

They generated lots of documentation across the whole stack and now makes all PO/BAs read it if it's correct. So not just 300 lines - he unironically generated thousands of lines of "documentation" and is now making hundreds of people review it for him

Complete brainrot

Au psychosis is getting seriously outrageous at this point

Thankfully I'm a dev and thus aren't in the blast radius of that genius idea
children.textZhHtml:
在我的日常工作中，有一个人在整个企业中领导人工智能。

他们在整个堆栈中生成了大量文档，现在让所有 PO/BA 阅读它（如果正确的话）。所以不仅仅是 300 行 - 他讽刺地生成了数千行“文档”，现在让数百人为他审阅

完全脑残

Au精神病在这一点上变得非常令人愤慨

谢天谢地，我是一名开发人员，因此不在那个天才想法的爆炸范围内

children.author: prymitive
children.textRawHtml:
I think a lot of that is people who were always very insecure because they’re mediocre engineers. Previously asking questions or not understanding something was a bit painful but now you can hear “you’re absolutely right!” and make progress all day every day.
Until you need to interact with actual humans and that’s why you try to minimise it, hiding behind ai generated content.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为很多人总是非常没有安全感，因为他们是平庸的工程师。以前提出问题或不理解某些事情会有点痛苦，但现在你可以听到“你完全正确！”并每天都取得进步。
直到你需要与真实的人类互动，这就是为什么你试图将其最小化，隐藏在人工智能生成的内容后面。

children.author: ungreased0675
children.textRawHtml: I’m not a developer, but when I watch devs whose work process is prompt, copy-paste, try to run, paste error into code, try to run, etc. I can’t help but think they’re unskilled. There’s no brain engagement, no understanding of the bigger picture, just being a worse slower agent.
children.textZhHtml: 我不是开发人员，但是当我看到开发人员的工作流程是提示性的、复制粘贴、尝试运行、将错误粘贴到代码中、尝试运行等等时，我不禁认为他们不熟练。没有大脑参与，没有对大局的理解，只是成为一个更慢的智能体。

children.author: jvanderbot
children.textRawHtml:
Sure, but even worse, is the state-of-the-art: they use a cli agent and the "copy-paste, try to run, paste error, try to run" loop is called "Agentic engineering." Now we have to believe they're 10/10?

I see no difference there except speed at the cost of whatever little understanding may have been gained by the manual inspection between steps.
children.textZhHtml:
当然，但更糟糕的是最先进的：他们使用 cli 代理，“复制粘贴，尝试运行，粘贴错误，尝试运行”循环被称为“代理工程”。现在我们必须相信它们是 10/10？

除了速度之外，我看不出有什么区别，但代价是通过步骤之间的手动检查可能获得了一点点理解。

children.author: kooi
children.textRawHtml:
Any competent developer knows there are limits to prompting.

Personally I've found LLM's suck at multi-threaded applications. (Because I've been tempted by the ~agentic loop~ and been burned. Then I hand code the core logic and all is well).

Woe to the developer who tries to prompt their way through this.
children.textZhHtml:
任何有能力的开发人员都知道提示是有限制的。

就我个人而言，我发现 LLM 在多线程应用程序方面很糟糕。 （因为我被〜代理循环〜诱惑并被烧毁。然后我手动编写了核心逻辑，一切都很好）。

那些试图提示他们解决这个问题的开发人员有祸了。

children.author: wuliwong
children.textRawHtml: I hit a wall with creating a browser based video editor. Up until then, over the last year, I have been taking my hands off the wheel more and more and really have just become more and more productive. This video editor experience has forced me to get more into the code again.
children.textZhHtml: 我在创建基于浏览器的视频编辑器时遇到了困难。到那时为止，在过去的一年里，我的双手越来越多地从方向盘上移开，并且确实变得越来越高效。这次视频编辑器的经历迫使我再次深入研究代码。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
Skill issue /s

But seriously, lots of apps are just glorified NextJS apps which have tons of training data. Something like rust would likely churn out nonsense that compiles eventually but isn't optimal.
children.textZhHtml:
技能问题/s

但说真的，很多应用程序只是美化的 NextJS 应用程序，它们拥有大量的训练数据。像 Rust 这样的东西可能会产生最终编译但不是最佳的废话。

children.author: tomtomtom777
children.textRawHtml:
I think the worst is when they are skilled.

You're basically describing my work day. My job went from interesting, highly skilled work to mostly horrible brain rot over the past year.

It's depressing and I don't know a way out. Other then a complete career change, throwing away 30 years of experience and a matching salary.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为最糟糕的是当他们熟练时。

你基本上是在描述我的工作日。在过去的一年里，我的工作从有趣的、高技能的工作变成了可怕的大脑腐烂。

这令人沮丧，我不知道出路。除此之外，还有一个彻底的职业转变，丢掉 30 年的经验和相匹配的薪水。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
Maybe it's because my org gave us permission to fail and make mistakes, but I transitioned to AI driven development pretty quickly and am having fun learning how to best drive the AI to produce good quality code, with harnesses and patterns to prevent mistakes and a process to learn and rollback. It's a different kind of engineering now. I find myself thinking more product level and system level than if else branches. I think I've been able to upskill in ways that I wouldn't have been able to if I were still writing code by hand, mainly because I have the bandwidth to do so now.

I only have 10 years of experience, so I'm not trying to say that your lived experience is invalid, but personally I figure if this is the way the industry is heading then I may as well try to learn how to thrive within the new environment.
children.textZhHtml:
也许是因为我的组织允许我们失败和犯错误，但我很快就过渡到了人工智能驱动的开发，并且很高兴学习如何最好地驱动人工智能生成高质量的代码，利用防止错误的工具和模式以及学习和回滚的过程。现在这是一种不同类型的工程。我发现自己比 if else 分支思考更多的产品级别和系统级别。我认为我已经能够以如果我仍然手工编写代码就无法提高技能的方式，主要是因为我现在有足够的带宽来这样做。

我只有 10 年的经验，所以我并不是想说你的生活经验无效，但我个人认为，如果这就是行业的发展方向，那么我不妨尝试学习如何在新环境中蓬勃发展。

children.author: ent001
children.textRawHtml:
This is my biggest problem with the current state of things. The loss in quality of life out weights the gains in productivity. And they are concentrated on highly conscientiousness individuals, those who already got silently taxed with most of the 80% of the work to get the last 20% of the results. So it is now compounding, if you care your workload will approximate 99,99..% of the total workload divided by the number of high conscientiousness individuals in your team/organization.

The current hype cycle might even represent a net global gain like some people argue. But it represents yet more externality driven exploitation. Remains to be seen what the new equilibrium will be given that now the population being exploited is not only close to the core of the world system but also already overburdened.

I do think it represents a mere acceleration of the previous trend that resulted since around 2005 in an explosion of average (not median) pay for software developers due to similar dynamics. If the system settles on a new level of pay that manages to convince enough people of enough skill to go along, it might just hum along and not implode. As for the rest of us, welcome to the growing permanent underclass and brace for the impact of the climate wars. We will be the fodder that will insulate the chosen ones under their air conditioned domes.
children.textZhHtml:
这是我目前的最大问题。生活质量的损失超过了生产力的提高。他们集中在高度尽责的个人身上，这些人已经默默地承担了 80% 工作的大部分，以获得最后 20% 的结果。因此，如果您关心的话，您的工作量将大约占总工作量的 99,99..%，除以您的团队/组织中高度责任心的个人数量。现在情况变得更加复杂。

当前的炒作周期甚至可能代表着一些人认为的全球净收益。但它代表了更多外部性驱动的剥削。鉴于现在被剥削的人口不仅接近世界体系的核心，而且已经负担过重，新的平衡将是什么还有待观察。

我确实认为这只是先前趋势的加速，这种趋势自 2005 年左右以来由于类似的动态导致软件开发人员的平均（而不是中位数）薪酬激增。如果这个系统确定了一个新的薪酬水平，能够说服足够多有足够技能的人去接受，它可能只会继续发展，而不是崩溃。至于我们其他人，欢迎不断壮大的永久下层阶级，并为气候战争的影响做好准备。我们将成为将被选中的人隔离在空调圆顶下的饲料。

children.author: pixl97
children.textRawHtml:
I mean, we're just the neo-luddites in this case. Or maybe the rust belt when jobs moved elsewhere.

The real question isn't if things are going to change around our jobs, its are we going to be able to move fast enough to avoid starving in the streets?
children.textZhHtml:
我的意思是，在这种情况下我们只是新勒德分子。或者也许是工作转移到其他地方时的铁锈地带。

真正的问题不是我们的工作周围的情况是否会发生变化，而是我们是否能够足够快地移动以避免在街上挨饿？

children.author: leptons
children.textRawHtml: I'm in the same boat as you... 30 years of experience writing software, and now I'm just supposed to click "approve" on PRs without reading the PR. I'm just supposed to press a button. I'm looking for a new job, but it's going to be difficult to find one in tech that isn't a complete AI-psychosis shitshow.
children.textZhHtml: 我和你的情况一样......拥有 30 年的软件编写经验，现在我应该在不阅读 PR 的情况下点击 PR 上的“批准”。我只需要按一个按钮。我正在寻找一份新工作，但在科技领域很难找到一份不完全是人工智能精神病狗屎的工作。

children.author: projectazorian
children.textRawHtml: This is a sign of poor harness configuration and/or org level constraints (lack of MCP support, etc.) With properly configured and prompted agents error copy-pasta should be the exception not the norm.
children.textZhHtml: 这是糟糕的线束配置和/或组织级别约束（缺乏 MCP 支持等）的标志。如果正确配置并提示代理错误，copy-pasta 应该是例外而不是常态。

children.author: mikebenfield
children.textRawHtml: I think I’m pretty skilled, or at least I was, but much of my work now looks like this. The fact is in many cases Claude can diagnose and fix the issue quicker than I can even read it. It would be crazy not to take advantage of this. Of course it does get hard to resist the temptation to just become ever lazier over time.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为我非常熟练，或者至少是这样，但我的大部分工作现在看起来都是这样的。事实上，在很多情况下，克劳德可以比我阅读它更快地诊断和解决问题。如果不利用这一点那就太疯狂了。当然，随着时间的推移，人们确实很难抗拒变得越来越懒的诱惑。

children.author: tdeck
children.textRawHtml:
This is my exact process nowadays when debugging some weird Linux wifi driver issue or something that came up after upgrade.

But that's because I don't have any real familiarity with the systems involved and I don't expect that gaining such familiarity will benefit me. If I am working on a system or product I'm responsible for at my job, it should be a different situation.
children.textZhHtml:
这就是我现在调试一些奇怪的 Linux wifi 驱动程序问题或升级后出现的问题时的具体过程。

但那是因为我对所涉及的系统没有任何真正的熟悉，而且我不认为获得这种熟悉会给我带来好处。如果我正在开发我在工作中负责的系统或产品，情况应该会有所不同。

children.author: xyproto
children.textRawHtml: It's also very easy to dismiss everyone falling into the "AI trap" as being mediocre in the first place, though. But one just can't know this without having seen their work pre-AI.
children.textZhHtml: 不过，我们也很容易认为每个落入“人工智能陷阱”的人一开始都是平庸的。但如果没有看过他们在人工智能出现之前的工作，就无法知道这一点。

children.author: bigfishrunning
children.textRawHtml: I think the "meat proxy" people are mediocre regardless of whether or not the were brilliant pre-AI. They've reduced themselves to a copy-paste go-between for claude and slack (or github or jira or whatever) and are mediocre now. If only they could turn back the clock...
children.textZhHtml: 我认为“肉类代理”的人都是平庸的，无论他们在人工智能出现之前是否辉煌。他们已经把自己沦为 claude 和 slack（或者 github 或 jira 等等）的复制粘贴中间人，现在表现平平。如果他们能让时光倒流就好了……
